note: Default fixed-seed scenario for the ADR-003 NDVI-vs-RGB spike (docs/SPIKE_ndvi_vs_rgb.md). SYNTHETIC STAND-IN, not a Gazebo render -- see sim/spike/README.md.

soil_patches.note: bare-ground hard case: bird_1 is scripted to cross this patch (false-negative risk for NDVI-direct)
background bare patch, no bird crosses it -- precision/FP texture only

shadow_patches.note: moderate NDVI depression (canopy shadow analog); no birds scripted through it in v1

clutter_blobs.note: static non-bird low-NDVI feature (e.g. mulch/exposed rock), bird-blob-sized -- false-positive test for naive NDVI threshold. bird_2 passes near but not on top of it.

birds.note: easy case: clean canopy background, mid-range (~10m below camera). Sanity baseline both approaches should catch. Transverse crossing (near-constant x) so it stays in-frame while the camera dwells over it.

hard case: crosses soil_0 (background NDVI ~0.15) at close range (~7m below camera) while bird NDVI is -0.08 -- low contrast against background. RGB stays high-contrast (grey bird on brown soil) -- this is the case the spike is designed to falsify (a) on. x held at the soil_0 center (65,20) so the whole transverse crossing stays over/at the patch edge.

far/small case (~13m below camera, smallest apparent radius) passing near (not over) clutter_0 at (92,15) -- tests range sensitivity and bird-vs-static-clutter discrimination (motion is the only distinguishing signal, since NDVI/RGB values are similar to the clutter blob). x held near clutter_0's x so both are in-frame together; y sweep stays >=2m off clutter_0's position (clutter r=1.0 + feather=0.4) so it never overlaps.
